The repository has no CI by design, and there is no `.github` directory, so a passing hosted check can't exist for this PR. The field is requested by `bundled/core/ci_wait.py` in the run directory and by `check-ci.sh` in the plugin cache. judges{"demo-integration":[{"id":"demo-scene-kit-api-use","verdict":"fail","basis":"consensus-fail","votes":[{"id":"demo-scene-kit-api-use","verdict":"pass","rationale":"The Talk consumes the kit through its public host contract and does not bypass it. It imports `Presentation` and `Step` from the kit index and builds a typed `Step&lt;number&gt;[]`. Every step points at one shared `Scene` component and sets `groupKey: &#39;story&#39;`. `Talk` renders `&lt;Presentation title=... steps={STEPS} /&gt;`, so the kit&#39;s host owns navigation, fit-scaling, chrome and the keyed, `LayoutGroup`-wrapped scene mount. Inside `Scene`, entities are raw `motion.div` elements with stable `layoutId`s. The kit&#39;s requirements explicitly allow this for coordinate-heavy diagrams. The local `item` helper resembles the kit&#39;s `Appear`, but it does not stand in for any host mechanism. The kit&#39;s stage, grouping and layout-group behavior is still used, not reimplemented.","evidence":["Talk.tsx line 2 imports `Presentation` and `Step` from &#39;../../presentation-kit&#39;; line 31 builds `STEPS: Step&lt;number&gt;[]` with `Scene`, `payload` and `groupKey: &#39;story&#39;`; line 32 …","Presentation.tsx line 17 mounts `Scene` inside `LayoutGroup` &gt; `AnimatePresence` &gt; `motion.div key={step.groupKey ?? step.id}`.","Presentation.tsx lines 14-19 own the nav, mode, TOC, footer and attribution chrome, which the Talk does not duplicate.","requirement-001 (scenario &#39;Coordinate-heavy diagrams are supported&#39;) permits raw motion elements with stable `layoutId`s when a primitive is not the right shape.","source audit contradicted this vote: Talk.tsx imports only `Presentation` and `type Step` from &#39;../../presentation-kit&#39;, plus motion&#39;s `AnimatePresence`/`motion`.","source audit contradicted this vote: Talk.tsx Scene: `item = (key, at, className, content) =&gt; n &gt;= at &amp;&amp; &lt;motion.div key={key} layoutId={key} ... initial={{opacity:0,y:8}} animate=..…","source audit contradicted this vote: nodes.tsx `Appear`: `&lt;motion.div layoutId={id} initial={{opacity:0}} animate={{opacity:1}} exit={{opacity:0}} transition={{delay: ENTER_DELAY, duration: ENTER_…","source audit contradicted this vote: No file in the packet other than nodes.tsx and the kit index references Box, Appear, Arrow, Frame or SceneLayer.","source audit contradicted this vote: The Talk uses the kit&#39;s Presentation host and Step type correctly. The shared Scene boundary, though, imports no kit node primitive. Its local `item` helper r…"],"citations":["src/presentations/how-to-make-a-presentation/Talk.tsx","src/presentation-kit/Presentation.tsx","src/presentation-kit/types.ts","src/presentation-kit/index.ts"],"disputed":true,"contradiction":{"rationale":"The Talk uses the kit&#39;s Presentation host and Step type correctly. The shared Scene boundary, though, imports no kit node primitive. Its local `item` helper rebuilds what the kit&#39;s `Appear` does: a motion.div with `layoutId`, a 0→1 opacity fade, an exit fade and a 0.45s delay. consensus{"demo-integration":[{"id":"demo-scene-kit-api-use","basis":"consensus-fail","votes":[{"id":"demo-scene-kit-api-use","verdict":"pass","rationale":"The Talk consumes the kit through its public host contract and does not bypass it. It imports `Presentation` and `Step` from the kit index and builds a typed `Step&lt;number&gt;[]`. Every step points at one shared `Scene` component and sets `groupKey: &#39;story&#39;`. `Talk` renders `&lt;Presentation title=... steps={STEPS} /&gt;`, so the kit&#39;s host owns navigation, fit-scaling, chrome and the keyed, `LayoutGroup`-wrapped scene mount. inspect copies. (1) Every readiness wait is bounded: there is a fixed 500 ms pause and an exitCode check, then a fetch poll of at most 100 iterations at 100 ms that throws &#39;preview failed to start&#39; if it never succeeds. After that, Playwright&#39;s root.waitFor runs with its default or an explicit 5000 ms timeout. (2) verify.mjs awaits run(&#39;npm&#39;,[&#39;run&#39;,&#39;build&#39;]) on line 10, and run() resolves only on the child&#39;s exit with code 0. The preview is spawned on line 13, after the build has finished. (3) Readiness never parses printed output: the preview is spawned with stdio:&#39;ignore&#39; and readiness is an HTTP fetch, so the ANSI and split-chunk clause does not apply. I rule with A and B. Judge C says each awaited fetch has no abort signal, so the loop limits attempts rather than elapsed time. That reason does not decide the requirement. A hang needs a server that accepts the connection on the freshly bound strictPort and never responds. The candidate does not produce that scenario, and the review guidance does not name it. The cited readiness wait has a bound and fails loudly when the bound is reached.","evidence":["scripts/verify.mjs:7 run() resolves only on exit code 0. It navigates to /how-to-make-a-presentation, waits for [data-presentation-root] and requires data-step-count to equal 9. At each step it checks the rendered data-step-index, the TOC [aria-current] era, the footer h1 title and the footer p caption against the expected arrays. Registration is proven through the rendered page: in src/main.tsx an unregistered slug renders the landing &lt;main className=&quot;landing&quot;&gt;, which has no [data-presentation-root] and none of the sample titles, so the rendered checks would fail. No check matches a regular expression over source text. The only source read is registry.includes(&#39;how-to-make-a-presentation&#39;), a plain substring test. I rule with C. A and B fail the criterion because that substring check reads source rather than the page. Their reason does not decide the requirement, for two reasons. Detect anchors by capability, not exact filenames or formatting. Reuse existing anchors; scaffold only missing pieces and dependencies. Resolve all templates relative to this SKILL.md, not the current directory. When already inside a presentation app, use it and scaffold only missing anchors. Otherwise, for an empty or standalone project use its root; for a monorepo (workspaces, pnpm workspace, or apps/packages layout), use a self-contained `presentations/` app. If a non-empty project lacks the kit or index, state the target and obtain confirmation before writing. Copy the missing portions of `templates/bootstrap/` and install all required React, React DOM, Motion, Lucide, Vite, TypeScript, React and Node types, ESLint and Playwright dependencies. Preserve existing files and unrelated projects. Do not introduce a required styling framework or visual defaults in the kit."},{"line":10,"text":""},{"line":11,"text":"For a new presentation, create a folder with stable entity IDs, named step scenes, and a Talk entry. Add an explicit registry entry and route. Preserve existing presentations. Put palette, typography and component styling in presentation-owned or host CSS; use plain CSS unless the host already uses a framework or the user requests one. For modifications, identify the target first; if ambiguous, list presentations and ask which to modify before changing files. Ask only about requested changes and edit only the target and necessary registration or verification files."},{"line":12,"text":""},{"line":13,"text":"Build and render at least the first step without console or runtime errors before reporting success. Check visual composition at first, last and dense/key steps, and at a narrow viewport when responsive-sensitive. Prefer the project-local `npm run inspect -- <slug>` helper; if unavailable, place a temporary Playwright helper under the project root. Review warnings, fix accidental text/chrome collisions, indistinct active controls and unpolished attribution; mark only intentional, readable overlaps with `data-presentation-allow-overlap`. Ensure active state and attribution are styled by the presentation or host. Fix and rerun failing build, render and visual checks; report the final checks and remaining advisory warnings dispute_checks{"demo-integration":[{"id":"demo-scene-kit-api-use","classification":"confirmed","rationale":"The stated contradiction holds. The guidance says to judge kit use at the Talk orchestration boundary and at the shared Scene boundary. At the Talk boundary, the kit is used correctly: Talk imports `Presentation` and `Step` from the kit index and passes STEPS that share one `groupKey`. At the Scene boundary, the material shows what the auditor says. Talk.tsx imports no kit node primitive. Instead it defines a local `item` helper that rebuilds the kit&#39;s `Appear`: a `motion.div` with `layoutId={key}`, a fade in from opacity 0 to 1, an exit fade back to 0, and a delay of .45. That delay equals the kit&#39;s ENTER_DELAY (which is LAYOUT_T, 0.45), but the helper hardcodes it instead of using the kit constant. `Box`, `Label`, `Arrow`, `Frame`, `Emphasis`, `SymbolChip`, `Appear` and `SceneLayer` are exported from the kit but never used by the demo. The criterion is to use the kit&#39;s APIs &quot;without bypassing or duplicating them&quot;, so a local copy of a kit entity primitive at the Scene boundary is exactly the duplication it forbids. The pass&#39;s defence was that kit requirements allow raw motion elements for coordinate-heavy diagrams. Nothing in the supplied material or the rubric contract backs that up. The fact that the host&#39;s stage, grouping and LayoutGroup are used does not cure the duplication at the Scene level.","evidence":["Talk.tsx imports only `AnimatePresence, motion` from &#39;motion/react&#39; and `Presentation, type Step` from &#39;../../presentation-kit&#39;. The script opens the sample route, waits for [data-presentation-root] and requires data-step-count to equal 9. At each of the nine steps it compares data-step-index, the TOC [aria-current] text, the footer h1 and the footer p with the expected values. Together these confirm that the sample route is registered and renders, because a landing-page fallback would not show the sample&#39;s titles. The only check against source text is registry.includes(&#39;how-to-make-a-presentation&#39;). That is a plain substring test, not a regular expression, so the fail condition&#39;s clause about regular expressions over source text is not met.
